technical_data.email_spoofing_technique: The attacker used a lookalike domain 'micr0soft-secure.com' replacing the letter 'o' with zero and configured SPF records to pass for their sending IPs but failed DKIM and DMARC authentication, causing the recipient system to quarantine or flag the email.

Received: from mail.micr0soft-secure.com (mail.micr0soft-secure.com [198.51.100.23]) by mx.yourcompany.com with ESMTPS

indicators: Domain name: micr0soft-secure.com (lookalike domain with '0' instead of 'o')
Email SPF pass but DKIM and DMARC fail
Email sender IP 198.51.100.23 not belonging to legitimate Microsoft IP ranges
Suspicious URL with query redirect to legitimate portal.office.com domain
Phishing page mimics Office365 login page with POST form to harvest credentials
User agent strings indicating automated or uncommon clients
SMTP logs showing direct mail submission from suspicious IPs
examples.detection_method: Use of advanced email filtering solutions that verify SPF, DKIM, and DMARC alignment combined with machine learning models analyzing domain age, URL reputation, and email content. Deploy sandboxing or URL rewriting to test destination pages. Monitor user reports and failed login attempts after phishing campaigns. Implement simulated phishing exercises with similar lookalike domains to train users. EDR and network proxy logs can detect POST requests to suspicious domains with credential submission.
